    Movies¶

    Are higher budget films more profitable? To answer this question, I analized data from the-numbers.com as of March 28, 2025.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

pd.options.display.float_format = '{:,.2f}'.format

from pandas.plotting import register_matplotlib_converters
register_matplotlib_converters()

    Descriptive Statistics¶

    Questions:

    1. What is the average production budget?
    2. What is the average worldwide gross revenue?
    3. What are the minima of domestic and worldwide gross revenues?
    4. Are the bottom 25% of movies profitable?
    5. What are the maxima of production budget and worldwide gross revenue?
    6. What are the worldwide gross revenues of the lowest and highest budget movies?
    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    desc = df.describe()
print(f"1. The average production budget is: ${desc['production_budget_usd'].loc['mean'].round(2):,}")
print(f"2. The average worldwide gross revenue is: ${desc['worldwide_gross_usd'].loc['mean'].round(2):,}")
print(f"3. The minimum of domestic gross revenues is: ${desc['domestic_gross_usd'].loc['min'].round(2):,}. The minimum of worldwide gross revenue is: ${desc['worldwide_gross_usd'].loc['min'].round(2):,}")
are_bp25_profitable = True if desc["worldwide_gross_usd"].loc["25%"] - desc["production_budget_usd"].loc["25%"] else False
print(f"4. The bottom 25% of movies are {'not ' if are_bp25_profitable else ''}profitable")
print(f"5. The maximum of production budgets is: ${desc['production_budget_usd'].loc['max'].round(2):,}. The maximum of worldwide gross revenues is: ${desc['worldwide_gross_usd'].loc['max'].round(2):,}")
highest_budget_movie = df.loc[df["production_budget_usd"] == df["production_budget_usd"].max()]
lowest_budget_movie = df.loc[df["production_budget_usd"] == df["production_budget_usd"].min()]
# highest_budget_movie["worldwide_gross_usd"].values[0]

      f"The highest budget movie has a revenue of {highest_budget_movie['worldwide_gross_usd'].values[0]:,}")

    Bubble Plots¶

    In [14]:
    Copied! 
    plt.figure(figsize=(8,4), dpi=200)
plt.title("Budget vs Income")
ax = sns.scatterplot(data=df, x="production_budget_usd", y="worldwide_gross_usd", hue="worldwide_gross_usd", size="worldwide_gross_usd")

ax.set(ylim= (0, df["worldwide_gross_usd"].max() * 1.05),
      xlim= (0,df["production_budget_usd"].max()),
       ylabel = "Income in $ billions",
       xlabel = "Budget in $100 millions"
      )

legend = ax.legend()
legend.set_title("Income USD")
for text in legend.get_texts():
    text.set_text(f"${float(text.get_text())/1e9:.2f}B")

ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f"{y/1e9:.1f}"))

ax.plot()

    Regression Model¶

    What is the estimated income of a movie with a budget of $500M?

    In [19]:
    Copied! 
    model = LinearRegression()
X = pd.DataFrame(new_movies, columns=["production_budget_usd"])
Y = pd.DataFrame(new_movies, columns=["worldwide_gross_usd"])
model.fit(X, Y)
theta0 = model.intercept_[0]
theta1 = model.coef_[0,0]
price = theta0 + theta1 * 500_000_000
print(f"The estimated income of a movie with a budget of $500M is ${round(price):,}")
    model = LinearRegression() X = pd.DataFrame(new_movies, columns=["production_budget_usd"]) Y = pd.DataFrame(new_movies, columns=["worldwide_gross_usd"]) model.fit(X, Y) theta0 = model.intercept_[0] theta1 = model.coef_[0,0] price = theta0 + theta1 * 500_000_000 print(f"The estimated income of a movie with a budget of $500M is ${round(price):,}")
